title: Shard-based usage republish protocol for VPC/offline collectors
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: In VPC/private deployments we regularly see windows where the control-plane cannot accept live telemetry (network maintenance, customer firewall rules, or intentional air-gapped export). During these windows on-prem collectors buffer and later attempt to ship usage. Existing ad-hoc bundling leads to two recurring issues: 1) missing events when a collector fails to replay a partial bundle, and 2) duplicate events when retries are not deduplicated by the control plane. Both cause billing inaccuracies and customer trust risk.

Proposed solution: implement a shard-based republish protocol for on-prem/VPC collectors that combines compact immutable snapshots + append-only delta windows. Each collector partitions usage into logical shards (tenant-day or tenant-range) and assigns monotonically increasing segment IDs. Clients ship two artifact types to the control plane over a secure channel or upload manifest: (A) snapshot (compact, signed summary of state with segment sequence numbers and a small Merkle-of-batches hash) and (B) delta segments (append-only lists of events with batch_id and segment_seq). The control plane will accept at-least-once deliveries but enforce idempotency using (tenant_id, shard_id, segment_seq) and a deterministic batch fingerprint. A small local dedup store on the collector (LRU cache keyed by batch fingerprint) plus segment tombstones enable safe GC.

Key design constraints: keep bandwidth low for air-gapped USB manifests; surfacing small human-readable manifests is required for compliance audits; ensure reconcilers can deterministically compute final counts from the sequence; tolerate out-of-order arrival; avoid global cross-tenant locks.

Success criteria: end-to-end accounting delta < 0.5% across synthetic workload tests and < 24h median reconciliation time after extended offline window; zero unreconciled segments older than 7 days in staging; per-tenant duplicate ratio < 0.01% in long-run tests.

Open questions: shard sizing for heavy multi-tenant hosts, retention/GC policy for dedup state, whether to require manifest signing via customer KMS vs. platform signing, and backwards compatibility with old collector bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Collectors produce signed manifests and segment artifacts that the control plane can replay deterministically
Replayed segments applied idempotently with no net duplicates for 99.99% of events in large-scale tests
System emits reconciliation metrics: segments_replayed, segments_duplicated, segments_missing, and time_to_reconcile
Provide an ops runbook for manual replay and dispute resolution
E2E test harness with synthetic offline window and randomized failures included in CI
design_notes: Sequence model: (tenant_id, shard_id, segment_seq) monotonic — segment_seq resets only when shard is rotated
Batch fingerprint: SHA256 of sorted event ids + metadata; control plane uses fingerprint for quick idempotency check
Manifest format: newline-delimited JSON list (for auditability) with per-shard merkle root and segment ranges
Fast path: when control plane reachable, collectors stream segments over TLS; when offline, create compressed delta segments and a manifest for later upload
Backoff: exponential backoff with jitter for retries and a lease-based reupload to avoid hot replays
GC: control plane keeps per-tenant applied segment_seq watermark and exposes a reclaim TTL configurable per-customer
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag on control plane to accept new artifact schema behind 'sharded_republish_v1'. 2) Release collector-side opt-in that can produce the new manifests in parallel with legacy bundles. 3) Run canary for 10 enterprise tenants (no billing) for 2 weeks and verify reconciliation metrics. 4) Gradual enable by customer opt-in; automatic fallback to legacy ingest if manifest signature verification fails.
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting and idempotency logic; integration test that simulates network partitions and replays; staging load test with 10k tenants generating out-of-order segments; property tests ensuring commutativity when segments are permuted; nightly consistency job that compares ledger vs. replayed snapshot counts.
migration_steps: Collectors: bump agent to v2 that can emit both legacy bundles and sharded manifests. Control plane: accept v2 artifacts and write to a staging queue before final ledger commit. Run parallel reconciliation for 2 billing cycles and compare results, then flip migration flag to consume only v2 artifacts.
ops_runbook: 1) Alert 'reconcile_high_missing' triggers when segments_missing > 0.5% over 6h. 2) For missing segments: request manifest from customer, attempt resubmit via secure channel. 3) For duplicates: run dedup sweep using batch_fingerprint and report affected invoices for manual review. 4) For signature failures: escalate to security team and disable vault integration for that tenant until resolved.
metrics_and_dashboard: dashboard: Private Telemetry -> Replays (per-tenant view) with links to last manifest and segments
security_implications: Collector manifests are potentially sensitive; require envelope encryption for manifest transfers and optional customer KMS signing. Ensure control plane validates signatures and restricts manifest upload endpoints to tenant-scoped tokens. Documented in Confluence (link below).
